title: QRÖMELIFE
excerpt: Quavo has released *QRÖMELIFE*, his third solo album, a 14-track record executive produced by Pharrell Williams and developed with him over more than a year and a half.
body:
Quavo has released *QRÖMELIFE*, his third solo album, a 14-track record executive produced by Pharrell Williams and developed with him over more than a year and a half. It follows 2023's *Rocket Power*, which was made much closer to Takeoff's death and carried that grief through nearly every part of the record. *QRÖMELIFE* is less single-minded. The loss has not disappeared, but the album leaves much more room for pleasure, family, ambition and the ordinary parts of life that kept moving around it.

Pharrell became the central collaborator during sessions that stretched from Louis Vuitton's headquarters in Paris to a yacht in Miami. Quavo has said the challenge was not to replace his established sound but to recover parts of it that had become less visible, especially the melodic flexibility that let him move between Migos records, solo singles and features without sounding locked into one mode. "Trance (Walk It Down)" shows that side clearly. Heavy low end and quick percussion push it toward the club, while the vocal stays loose and melodic instead of turning every bar into a hard rhythmic attack. It is the kind of performance Pharrell had been pushing him to trust again.

The title comes from Quavo's own use of the word "qrome," which he connects to "chromosome." He uses it to describe the state of carrying something difficult while still getting up and handling everyday life. His example is ordinary. A person can go through a loss or crisis and still have to show up for work the next morning. In that definition, qrome is not a clean recovery story or a claim that the difficult part is over. For Quavo, the word describes living with the damage rather than pretending it has been left behind.

[apple:album:6817200688]

"Away" reunites Quavo and Offset on record after the public split that preceded Takeoff's death. The two repaired their relationship in the years that followed, and they are now sorting through ideas for another Migos project. Quavo has been careful about what continuing the group would mean without its third member. He says the chemistry with Offset is still there, but any future Migos release would have to honor Takeoff and his estate rather than simply continue under the name because the two surviving members can.

Most of *QRÖMELIFE* stays focused on Quavo's solo voice instead of turning that reunion into the album's main event. Familiar Atlanta rhythms are still there, but he sounds more interested in stretching his delivery than recreating a specific Migos era. Pharrell's influence is strongest when it leaves room for that instinct, letting the record move from harder drums into brighter melodic passages without making each change feel like a separate experiment. Compared with *Rocket Power*, the music is more relaxed because Quavo no longer asks every song to carry the full emotional weight of Takeoff's death.

The most personal change since *Rocket Power* happened outside music. Quavo recently revealed that he has become a father to a daughter and has spoken about how seriously he takes the role because his own father died when he was four. He wants to be present for the parts of his child's life that he never had a father there to see. The short film released with *QRÖMELIFE* moves through old Migos footage, Takeoff, studio sessions and the years that followed before ending with Quavo holding his daughter. The film stops there, with a father who lost his own at four holding the child he now plans to raise differently.
